description: We’re students from INHA University in Tashkent, combining AI, software engineering, 3D graphics, and immersive technologies to build Still Here — Voices Beyond Earth. Our platform reimagines NASA's open mission data as an interactive universe where users can experience the history of space exploration through virtual reality, AI-guided storytelling, and realistic mission simulations. We believe the future of STEM education begins when students don't just learn about space—they experience it.
summary:
Still Here gives a voice to six NASA machines that finished their missions and were left behind on the Moon and Mars: the Apollo 11 descent stage Eagle; the rovers Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity; the Ingenuity helicopter; and the InSight lander.

On a website (also usable as a Telegram Mini App), people can read each machine's story and drive a rover through its last chapter. In a Telegram bot, they can write to a machine and get an answer in the first person. Every answer is built only on a fixed list of facts taken from NASA mission pages. The project turns mission data into short, quiet, personal stories, so that people of any age remember these machines as part of the history of exploration, not as debris.
details:
What it does

  • Website / Telegram Mini App (https://space-x.mzmpro.uz) — a "space museum": a story page for each of the six machines; pages about the wider universe; and a Drive section with two interactive 3D chapters.
    • Opportunity: drive across Meridiani Planum, visit sites with fact cards, get stuck in soft sand, deal with dust on the solar panels, and end in the 2018 dust storm when power runs out.
    • Lunar Rover: the Apollo 17 Lunar Roving Vehicle in the Taurus-Littrow valley. A fender breaks, the crew repairs it, finds orange soil at Shorty crater, and finally the rover's camera watches the ascent stage lift off. This vehicle is not one of the six talking machines.
    • Controls: tap or click the ground, or use W A S D on a keyboard.
  • Telegram bot (@Yolgiz_ovoz_bot): the user picks a machine; the bot sends a short looping clip of that machine with its first-person introduction, plus buttons "Read my story" (opens the site) and "Other voices". After that, the user can write anything and the machine answers in 2–5 short sentences. The bot interface is English; the machine answers in the language the person writes in (for example English, Russian or Uzbek). Commands: /machines, /about, /reset.
  • API (FastAPI): serves the machine list and details; accepts short farewell notes to a machine and returns a short AI reply in the machine's voice; counts the messages each machine has received.

How it works

  • Each machine has a short list of verified facts (dates, distances, how the mission ended).
  • The AI receives only the facts of the one machine it plays, plus strict rules: every number, date and name must come from the facts; no invented events and no calculated numbers; the mission ending only as stated in the facts; the machine is no longer working, so no present activity.
  • If the AI is unavailable, the machine answers with prepared lines written from the same facts.
  • The famous line "My battery is low and it's getting dark" is explicitly marked as a journalist's paraphrase, never a real transmission from Opportunity.

Privacy and safety

  • The bot stores only the Telegram chat id. Logs contain no message texts and no IP addresses.
  • Requests are rate-limited and there is a daily per-chat limit for AI answers.
  • The machine stays in character and refuses unrelated tasks.
  • The audience includes children: no frightening or inappropriate content. If someone seems to be in distress, the machine steps out of the role and suggests talking to a trusted person.

Goals and audience

  • Goal: make people feel why these machines matter, using real data and a human, emotional story.
  • Audience: students, children, families and anyone curious about space, on phones, inside Telegram or in a browser.

Stack and tools

  • Backend: Python 3.12, FastAPI, aiogram 3 (Telegram bot, long polling), SQLite (aiosqlite), Pydantic, httpx.
  • Testing and linting: pytest, ruff.
  • Frontend: React 19, TanStack Start, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Radix UI, Framer Motion, three.js (3D drive), Telegram Web App API.
  • Deployment: Docker and Docker Compose with three services (api, bot, web) behind one domain.
  • Video: ffmpeg was used to make silent looping clips for the bot.Use of AI (Super Intelligence)
  • Lovable (AI website builder) generated the frontend (design, pages and components), which the team then integrated and adjusted. It also generated three images on the site (black-hole.jpg, earth-cover.jpg, mars-rover.jpg).
  • Claude Code (Anthropic) wrote the code: the backend (API, Telegram bot, database, prompts, tests, Docker setup, documentation) and the integration of the site with Telegram and the API. Shermukhammad Karimov built the 3D Drive chapters with Claude Code (Claude Fable 5.2).
  • Claude Haiku 4.5 (Anthropic) writes the machines' answers in the bot and the replies to farewell notes, called through an OpenAI-compatible API gateway. It receives only the facts of one machine, taken from the NASA sources listed in NASA Data, and rules that forbid inventing numbers, dates or events. If it fails, prepared lines written from the same facts are used. The bot's /about text says: "The voices of the machines are written by AI, based on real NASA mission data. The facts are real. The feelings are imagined."
  • Google Flow (AI video generation) made all the short looping clips in the bot: the welcome clip and one for each of the six machines. They are not NASA footage.
  • Visible watermarks: every AI-generated image on the site and every clip in the bot carries a visible "AI-generated" label in the picture itself.
  • No NASA branding in generated content: generated images, clips and 3D models contain no NASA logos, flags or mission identifiers. Mission text in the Opportunity clip was blurred, and the flag was removed from the 3D lunar module.
  • People checked every fact against NASA pages. The AI does not add facts.
